Bill number: HB2027
<bill_text>
HOUSE BILL 2027

 By White

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to physical activity.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-1021(b)(1), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (1) Physical activity may include:

 (A) Walking, jumping rope, playing volleyball, or other forms of physical

 activity that promote fitness and well-being;

 (B) Structured movement breaks; and

 (C) Time spent by a student in a physical education class if during such

 time the students are physically active.

 (2) Walking to and from class is not physical activity for purposes of this section.

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-1021(b)(2)(A)(ii), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (ii) Does not include time during which a student is permitted to use an electronic

 device; and

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-1021(b)(2)(B), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (B) A teacher may prevent a student from participating in physcial activity to

 improve the student's behavior.

 SECTION 4. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it, and

applies to the 2026-2027 school year and each school year thereafter.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill proposes changes to the definition and administration of physical activity in schools. It defines physical activity to include walking, jumping rope, playing volleyball, other activities that promote fitness and well-being, structured movement breaks, and time in physical education class when students are physically active. It specifies that walking to and from class does not count as physical activity. Additionally, the bill states that physical activity does not include time when a student is allowed to use an electronic device. The proposal also allows a teacher to prevent a student from participating in physical activity to improve that student's behavior. These changes would take effect July 1, 2026, for the 2026-2027 school year and beyond.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: It defines physical activity to include walking, jumping rope, playing volleyball, other activities that promote fitness and well-being
assessments.rationale: Conveys the listed activities and the fitness-and-well-being qualification for other activities.
Explicitly includes structured movement breaks in the list of qualifying physical activities.

assessments.summary_quote: time in physical education class when students are physically active
assessments.rationale: Preserves the condition that physical education class time counts only when students are physically active.

assessments.summary_quote: It specifies that walking to and from class does not count as physical activity.
assessments.rationale: Expressly conveys the exclusion of walking to and from class.

assessments.summary_quote: Additionally, the bill states that physical activity does not include time when a student is allowed to use an electronic device.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the electronic-device exclusion but omits the amendment target, Section 49-6-1021(b)(2)(A)(ii). That target is material because the supplied replacement fragment does not independently identify what the exclusion modifies.

assessments.summary_quote: The proposal also allows a teacher to prevent a student from participating in physical activity to improve that student's behavior.
assessments.rationale: Preserves the teacher's authority, the restriction on student participation, and its behavioral purpose.

assessments.summary_quote: These changes would take effect July 1, 2026, for the 2026-2027 school year and beyond.
assessments.rationale: Conveys both the effective date and application to the 2026-2027 school year and subsequent school years.
